header:
Date: 2026-07-30 | Start: 15:00 UTC | Duration: 62 minutes
Attendees: Samir (Redwood AE), Laura (Redwood SE), Rita (Redwood CSM); Maya (Apollo), Daniel (Apollo), Olivia (Apollo SRE), Ethan (Apollo Infra)
summary: Postmortem follow-up: review of July 24th incident where customer-facing Redwood Dedicated cluster experienced degraded tail latency during evening batch jobs. Discussed root causes (KV cache eviction patterns + autoscaler interaction), mitigations, short-term patch, and proposed reliability improvements + pilot for a config change. Agreed next steps around logs handoff, config proposal, and pilot SLA update.
transcript:
[00:00] Samir: ok everyone thanks for joining, we'll keep this to about an hour. quick recap: this is a follow-up to the outage on July twenty fourth where a subset of requests hit high tail latency. Laura and I will walk through the what we saw and the proposed mitigations. Maya, do you want to start with anything from your side?
[00:22] Maya: yeah thanks Samir. um to be clear it was impacting our clinical search UI, so it was high visibility. we saw timeouts at the edge around 20 seconds, and some requests retried and caused duplication. our SLOs are 95th under 600ms in normal times so this was a big hit.
[00:44] Laura: yeah and from Redwood's side we saw contended GPU memory on the dedicated pool and also a burst of long-context requests that invalidated large parts of the KV cache. the autoscaler also triggered node replacement which coincided w/ a cache rebuild.
[01:10] Daniel: are we confident it's the KV cache rebuild + autoscaler overlap? i mean i want to avoid chasing the wrong root cause.
[01:25] Laura: high confidence, there's a correlation in timestamps. we captured the memory pressure events followed by cache eviction logs. also, the batch jobs at 02:00 UTC had longer sequences and caused continuous batching to group them, which increased memory usage.
[01:52] Olivia: we also saw increased API retries from our side, those amplified the load. some of the retries were due to client-side timeouts at 5s and then exponential backoff that didn't kick in quickly.
[02:12] Samir: right ok, so root causes are multi-factor: long-context batch jobs, cache eviction, autoscaler node churn, and retry amplification. the good news: reproducible in our staging when we replayed the exact workload and sequence lengths.
[02:38] Maya: can you remind us what the short-term mitigation you already rolled was?
[02:45] Laura: we applied a hotfix on the runtime to increase KV cache retention threshold from 30% to 50% and paused autoscaler for the critical pool during the evening batch window. that reduced the cache rebuilds. latency dropped back to within expected margins in staging.
[03:10] Ethan: pausing autoscaler in prod concerns us from a capacity/cost perspective — curious on a more permanent fix.
[03:22] Rita: yeah that was a temporary emergency measure; we don't recommend that as long-term. the proposal is twofold: change batching/sequence routing + smarter autoscaler policy (delay scale-down when cache miss rate high).
[03:42] Daniel: ok show me the numbers.
[03:45] Laura: sure, here's a quick chart we shared prior to the call (link): tail latency peaked at ~6s, 95th at 1.8s during the event, request rate held roughly constant but CPU/GPU memory usage spiked. in the replay test where we increased KV retention and adjusted batching to avoid grouping long sequences with short ones, 95th returned to ~580ms and tail to ~1.1s.
[04:30] Maya: are there any tradeoffs for increasing cache retention? does it increase memory footprint or evictions elsewhere?
[04:40] Laura: yes it increases memory footprint on the serving nodes, which could reduce concurrent throughput if memory becomes saturated. that's why we pair it with batching policy changes and quantization profile adjustments to reduce per-token memory.
[05:00] Samir: we should also talk about monitoring and alerts — currently threshold is a naive percent based alarm, we recommend adding a rolling-window anomaly detector on cache miss rate and an alert when miss rate + scale events co-occur.
[05:25] Olivia: that would help. our concern is false positives. can you make it high precision?
[05:33] Laura: yes we can tune sensitivity and start in a monitoring-only mode for a week.
[05:40] [06:00] Samir: quick question on the pilot SLA — customer asked for a brief SLA addendum for reserve capacity in the evening window. Maya, do you want to recap?
[06:12] Maya: yes we asked if Redwood can guarantee a minimum of X throughput / reserved GPU for the 01:00-04:00 UTC window for 90 days while we test the config.
[06:25] Samir: we can draft an addendum offering reserved capacity with a rollback clause if it affects cost materially. we'll need sign-off from legal.
[06:36] Daniel: fine as long as it's time-boxed.
[06:40] [10:05] Laura: next topic: longer-term reliability improvements. proposed items: 1) smarter autoscaler that is cache-aware; 2) workload-aware routing so long sequences get pinned to nodes with larger KV warm caches; 3) improved retry semantics and client-side guidance; 4) scheduled compacting/eviction maintenance outside peak windows.
[10:40] Maya: the routing idea sounds good — will that require model variants or any changes to our app?
[10:48] Laura: minimal changes; mostly on the Redwood side tagging requests by expected sequence-length and routing based on node profiles. SDK can add an optional header.
[11:05] Ethan: any latency impact for short requests that get rerouted?
[11:12] Laura: negligible, routing decision is O(1) and we can use local routing tables. default remains best-effort on cluster.
[11:30] [15:00] Olivia: on the security/compliance side we noted audit logs were intact but some of the node replacement metadata was delayed; can you ensure replacements emit logs sooner?
[15:12] Samir: yes we'll forward the engineering ticket to infra and add tighter log flush on node lifecycle events.
[15:25] Laura: another point — quantization profile. for the Apollo model we recommended moving from 8-bit dynamic to a mixed 6/8 profile for embeddings-heavy endpoints. that reduced memory and improved throughput in staging.
[16:00] Daniel: any accuracy regression? for clinical search we can't accept degradation above 0.5% top-k.
[16:12] Laura: benchmark showed 0.12% delta on top-5 for the sample eval — within bounds. we'll include the full eval spreadsheet in the follow-up.
[16:35] Maya: about retries — we fixed some of our client timeouts but want Redwood guidance on server-side guidance to avoid retry storms.
[16:45] Samir: recommended pattern: 1) return 429 on transient overload with Retry-After header; 2) set server-suggested backoff in SDK; 3) Redwood to expose request-cost headers so you can preemptively throttle heavy requests.
[17:10] Olivia: okay that helps.
[17:20] [25:00] Laura: i want to call out an interesting edge case — when cache rebuilds happen and long requests are queued, they cause other shorter requests to face increased latency because of kernel scheduling on GPU. we proposed a scheduling priority that favors short tail-latency sensitive requests.
[25:40] Daniel: priority scheduling sounds complex, but useful. cost implications?
[25:50] Laura: minimal — it's a scheduler policy update not additional hardware. may require some perf tuning.
[26:10] Samir: let's map owners: Laura will own the config proposal & test plan; Samir will own the pilot SLA addendum and legal loop; Olivia/Ethan to provide replay dataset and access; Maya/Customer to confirm success criteria for the pilot.
[26:40] [35:00] Maya: success criteria recap: 95th under 700ms during the window for two weeks of replayed traffic, no more than one P95 spike over 1.5s in that period, and no user-facing errors.
[35:20] Daniel: acceptable.
[35:30] Samir: good. next — scheduling: Laura will run the controlled replay on your staging cluster on 2026-08-04, Samir will provision reserved capacity for pilot starting 2026-08-10 if we greenlight.
[36:00] [45:00] Laura: quick note: in staging we saw two small transcription errors in the logs where model names were truncated (redwood-model-v1 -> redwood-ml-v1) — it's an onboarding parsing bug, low priority but we'll fix.
[45:18] Maya: thanks. one question on billing: will reserved capacity be billed pro-rata for the day?
[45:30] Samir: yes standard reserved capacity billing applies, we'll include options (monthly vs daily blocks) in the proposal.
[45:45] Ethan: can we get a cost estimate for the recommended config changes (increased KV retention + reserved evening pool + quantization changes)?
[46:00] Samir: Laura will include a cost delta table in the config proposal.
[46:12] [55:00] Olivia: any outstanding risks we haven't covered?
[55:10] Laura: risk of inaccurate sequence-length prediction leading to misrouting; we'll mitigate with conservative thresholds and A/B test the header. also ops complexity from more autoscaler hooks, but acceptable.
[55:40] Maya: ok that seems reasonable. thanks for the thoroughness.
[56:00] Samir: recap of next steps: 1) Samir share incident timeline + raw logs by 2026-08-03; 2) Laura config proposal + cost delta + test plan by 2026-08-06; 3) Apollo provide replay dataset and access by 2026-08-02; 4) legal sign-off on pilot SLA by 2026-08-10. we'll sync after initial staging run.
[56:45] Daniel: noted.
[57:00] Maya: one final ask — can Redwood provide a short runbook for on-call to avoid taking that emergency pause in autoscaler next time?
[57:12] Rita: yes we'll draft an on-call runbook with steps and who to notify, include the quick temporary mitigations and a checklist.
[57:25] Samir: perfect, thanks everyone. we'll follow up in email with links to the logs and the proposal. meeting adjourned.
[62:00] End of recording.
